disease_label_per_paper: Typhoid intestinal perforation with 24 perforations in the ileum and cecum
presentation_summary: 35-year-old man was admitted with fever for 2 weeks, abdominal pain and vomiting for 4 days, abdominal distension for 2 days, and constipation for 2 days.
He had received no treatment during the 2-week febrile illness.
Exam showed a tense, tender, distended abdomen with absent bowel sounds, guarding and rigidity throughout the abdomen, and empty rectum on digital rectal examination.
Upright abdominal radiograph showed free gas under both hemidiaphragms; abdominal ultrasound showed free fluid and free air with fine floating echoes.

Exploratory laparotomy found fecal peritonitis and 24 perforations, 21 in terminal ileum and 3 in cecum; stool culture later grew S. typhi and histopathology was consistent with typhoid enteric perforation.
